description: The first benchmark is the mean unfilled quantity over all execution records.

a.request: Using the order executions, find each order's (`ordersmark`) average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`), ignoring missing values; executions with no order reference count together as one order. Take the mean unfilled quantity across all individual execution records, and keep the orders whose average is above it, noting how far above it they are. Among those orders, take the mean of their averages, keep only the orders above that mean as well, and note how far above it they are. Return one row with three values, without rounding: the average of the remaining orders' averages, their average excess over the first benchmark, and their average excess over the second.
a.sql: WITH avg_by_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) as avg_remain FROM orderexecutions WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ordersmark), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(remaincount) as overall_mean FROM orderexecutions WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL), first_filter AS (SELECT abo.ordersmark, abo.avg_remain, (abo.avg_remain - om.overall_mean) as excess_1 FROM avg_by_order abo CROSS JOIN overall_mean om WHERE abo.avg_remain > om.overall_mean), second_benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(avg_remain) as second_mean FROM first_filter), final_filter AS (SELECT ff.ordersmark, ff.avg_remain, ff.excess_1, (ff.avg_remain - sb.second_mean) as excess_2 FROM first_filter ff CROSS JOIN second_benchmark sb WHERE ff.avg_remain > sb.second_mean) SELECT AVG(avg_remain) as final_average, AVG(excess_1) as avg_excess_1, AVG(excess_2) as avg_excess_2 FROM final_filter

c.request: Using the order executions, find each order's (`ordersmark`) average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`), ignoring missing values; executions with no order reference count together as one order. Which orders are above the overall average unfilled quantity, and by how much? Among those orders, keep only the ones that are also above the group's own average, and note how far above it they are. Return one row with three values, without rounding: the average of these orders' averages, their average excess over the overall average, and their average excess over the second average. The first benchmark is the mean unfilled quantity over all execution records.
c.sql:
WITH all_executions AS (
  SELECT remaincount
  FROM orderexecutions
  WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL
),
order_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    ordersmark,
    AVG(remaincount) as order_avg
  FROM orderexecutions
  WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ordersmark
),
overall_avg_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(remaincount) as overall_average
  FROM all_executions
),
above_overall AS (
  SELECT order_avg
  FROM order_averages oa
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg_calc
  WHERE oa.order_avg > overall_avg_calc.overall_average
),
second_avg_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_avg) as second_average
  FROM above_overall
),
final_orders AS (
  SELECT ao.order_avg
  FROM above_overall ao
  CROSS JOIN second_avg_calc
  WHERE ao.order_avg > second_avg_calc.second_average
)
SELECT 
  AVG(fo.order_avg) as avg_of_averages,
  AVG(fo.order_avg - oac.overall_average) as avg_excess_overall,
  AVG(fo.order_avg - sac.second_average) as avg_excess_second
FROM final_orders fo
CROSS JOIN overall_avg_calc oac
CROSS JOIN second_avg_calc sac

b.request: Group executions by ordersmark (treating NULL ordersmark as one order), calculate each order's average remaincount (excluding NULL values), identify orders exceeding the global mean remaincount, compute the mean of these filtered orders' averages, identify orders within that group exceeding this secondary mean, and return three values: the average of these final orders' averages, the average of their individual excesses above the global mean, and the average of their individual excesses above the secondary mean.
b.sql: WITH order_averages AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) as avg_remaincount FROM orderexecutions WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ordersmark), global_mean_calc AS (SELECT AVG(remaincount) as global_mean FROM orderexecutions WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL), filtered_by_global AS (SELECT oa.ordersmark, oa.avg_remaincount, gm.global_mean FROM order_averages oa CROSS JOIN global_mean_calc gm WHERE oa.avg_remaincount > gm.global_mean), secondary_mean_calc AS (SELECT AVG(avg_remaincount) as secondary_mean FROM filtered_by_global), filtered_by_secondary AS (SELECT fbg.avg_remaincount, fbg.global_mean, sm.secondary_mean FROM filtered_by_global fbg CROSS JOIN secondary_mean_calc sm WHERE fbg.avg_remaincount > sm.secondary_mean) SELECT AVG(avg_remaincount) as metric_1, AVG(avg_remaincount - global_mean) as metric_2, AVG(avg_remaincount - secondary_mean) as metric_3 FROM filtered_by_secondary
b.raw: Group executions by ordersmark (treating NULL ordersmark as one order), calculate each order's average remaincount (excluding NULL values), identify orders exceeding the global mean remaincount, compute the mean of these filtered orders' averages, identify orders within that group exceeding this secondary mean, and return three values: the average of these final orders' averages, the average of their individual excesses above the global mean, and the average of their individual excesses above the secondary mean.

d.request: For each order (ordersmark), calculate the average unfilled quantity (remaincount) excluding nulls; identify orders exceeding the overall mean remaincount across all executions; from those, select only orders exceeding their group's own mean; return the mean of these selected orders' averages, their mean excess over the overall average, and their mean excess over their group's average.
d.sql:
WITH order_avgs AS (
  SELECT 
    ordersmark,
    AVG(remaincount) as avg_remain
  FROM orderexecutions
  WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ordersmark
),
overall_mean_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(remaincount) as overall_mean
  FROM orderexecutions
  WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL
),
above_overall AS (
  SELECT 
    oa.ordersmark,
    oa.avg_remain,
    o.userlink
  FROM order_avgs oa
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean_calc omc
  INNER JOIN orders o ON oa.ordersmark = o.recordvault
  WHERE oa.avg_remain > omc.overall_mean
),
user_group_means AS (
  SELECT 
    userlink,
    AVG(avg_remain) as user_group_mean
  FROM above_overall
  GROUP BY userlink
),
final_filtered AS (
  SELECT 
    ao.avg_remain,
    ugm.user_group_mean,
    omc.overall_mean
  FROM above_overall ao
  INNER JOIN user_group_means ugm ON ao.userlink = ugm.userlink
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean_calc omc
  WHERE ao.avg_remain > ugm.user_group_mean
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_remain) as mean_of_selected_averages,
  AVG(avg_remain - overall_mean) as mean_excess_over_overall,
  AVG(avg_remain - user_group_mean) as mean_excess_over_group
FROM final_filtered
